exposure: Trypanosoma cruzi infection status in women
history of living in infested houses (vector exposure)
outcome: congenital transmission of T. cruzi to infants
T. cruzi infection status in infants
cohort: The study included 1696 women, 456 of whom were infected with Trypanosoma cruzi, and their infants, from Bolivia.
finding: Sustained domestic vector exposure was associated with increased Chagas cardiomyopathy risk in women but decreased maternal parasitemia and congenital transmission risk, while higher maternal parasite loads and twin births independently increased congenital transmission.
